Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: An institutional records office processes intake forms by validating requester identity, matching document serial numbers to a central ledger, and routing signed approvals through designated supervisory channels. Each record carries a date-stamped custody log and a hash of the source file to maintain chain of evidence.

2) What occurred: On day one, the actor filed a request referencing building permit P-4412, leaving the inspector verification field unverified. On day two, the actor accessed the inspection file record F-9981, altering the violation status field while the compliance check remained unverified. On day three, the actor submitted payment document D-7720 through the secondary channel, leaving the account reconciliation sign-off unverified. On day four, the actor modified the date field on record F-9981, leaving the audit trail timestamp check unverified.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the central records database via a supervisor account. Payment document D-7720 was processed through the secondary remittance channel. Inspection file F-9981 was edited in the document management system.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Anomalous timestamp sequence on record F-9981. Payment D-7720 routed through non-standard channel. Unverified inspector field on permit P-4412. Account activity outside normal hours.
